findings.diagnosis: The prompt treats as safe cuts that split a copula/auxiliary (possibly negated) from the short complement that completes its predicate, so the prefix translates as a standalone claim that the continuation then contradicts.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_44','en_us_655','en_us_1081','en_us_733','en_us_738','en_us_1116'] — these cases all show a cut placed between a copula/auxiliary (is/was/will/does/had) and a short PP/locative/temporal/measurement or complement that completes the predicate.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences where a copula or auxiliary verb (is/are/was/were/has/have/will/does/etc.), possibly with a negator, is immediately (within about four tokens) followed by a short prepositional, locative, temporal, measurement, or complement phrase that completes the predicate.

edit.text: Do not cut between a copula/auxiliary (with optional negation) and its immediately following complement — a short PP/locative/temporal/measurement phrase or clause that completes the predicate.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that separate numerals from their units or measurement phrases, producing fragments that cannot be reliably translated or that invert meaning when rejoined.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_44','en_us_101','en_us_140'] — each shows a numeral (e.g. 105, 55,000, 240) separated from its unit/measurement phrase or parenthetical conversion.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences containing a numeral (digit or spelled-out) immediately followed by its unit or measurement phrase (including parenthetical unit conversions) without intervening punctuation.

edit.text: Do not cut between a numeral and its unit/measurement phrase (including parenthetical unit conversions).

findings.diagnosis: The prompt permits cuts inside noun phrases that separate a head noun from a restrictive post‑nominal modifier (of‑phrase, noun‑noun compound, or other essential modifier), producing ambiguous or unanchored fragments.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_360','en_us_1253','en_us_399'] — each example cuts the head noun away from an immediately following restrictive modifier (quoted technical name, 'of' phrase, or compound) that identifies the noun.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences where a noun is immediately followed by a restrictive post‑nominal modifier (an 'of' phrase, essential noun‑noun compound, quoted technical name, or restrictive clause) that identifies or scopes the head noun.

edit.text: Do not cut between a noun and an immediately following restrictive post‑nominal modifier (of‑phrase, noun‑noun compound, quoted name, or essential relative).
